Bayesian temperature reconstructions with a second predictor

Source: R/rec.ion.bayesian.R
rec.ion.bayesian.Rd

Reconstructs temperatures (in degrees C) from the posterior draws of cal.ion.bayesian(), the measured D47, and the Ion value of each sample.

Usage

rec.ion.bayesian(calModel, recData, ndraws = 10000, useIonError = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

calModel

Posterior draws from cal.draws(), a result from cal.ion.bayesian(), or the stanfit in it.

recData

The reconstruction dataset. It needs the columns Sample, D47, D47error (1 SD of the D47 value), and Ion. It also needs IonError (1 SD of Ion) when useIonError = TRUE.

ndraws

Number of draws used for each sample.

useIonError

Whether to account for the error in Ion.

...

Arguments from earlier versions (iter, postcalsamples, and MC). They are ignored.

Value

A data.frame with meanTemp (posterior mean, in degrees C) and error (1 SD) for each sample. The error includes uncertainty in the calibration parameters, the residual SD of the calibration (sigma), D47error, and IonError when used.

Details

With flat priors on 10^6/T^2 and Ion, the posterior of Ion follows its measurement, and the posterior of 10^6/T^2 for each draw is normal. Both are sampled directly, so no MCMC run is needed. Draws with 10^6/T^2 at or below zero are not physically possible. They are removed with a warning.
